newsitem.title: UK: UK stocks seen edgy ahead of Budget, U.S. FOMC.
newsitem.headline: UK stocks seen edgy ahead of Budget, U.S. FOMC.

text.p: Britain's FTSE 100 index was expected to open mixed to lower on Tuesday amid continuing nervousness ahead of the Labour government's first budget and caution ahead of the U.S. FOMC meeting.
"It looks like we'll have a mixed start, trending easier," said the head of equity sales at one brokerage.
"We'll struggle on any rally," another senior trader said.

On Monday the FTSE 100 index finished down 35 points at 4,604.6. "It was a bad performance by the FTSE yesterday, having been up 20 points we finished through the floor," the trader said. Pre-budget jitters were likely to limit activity, he said.
"Nobody wants to do anything at the moment," the trader said. "Everyone is worrying about the budget and Tokyo was knocked by talk that U.S. rates could go up.
The Nikkei 225 fell 2.08 percent, or 429 points, to 20,175 on Tuesday after stronger-than-expected U.S. data at the start of the week helped to dampen sentiment.

The Dow, meanwhile, finished just 15-points easier at 7,672.79 ahead of the two-day policy-making meeting which kicks off today. The U.S. index had been down 35 points as London markets closed. Most economists, however, still expect U.S. rates to be left unchanged this time around.

Interest rate concerns were also weighing on the domestic market following bumper consumer credit and money supply figures on Monday which sent UK gilts tumbling. UK monetary authorities are scheduled to meet next week to discuss for their regular policy meeting.
"As soon as this budget is over the market will be watching Eddie George to see what he makes of this," said the equity salesman. "Eddie George is very afraid of overshooting inflation targets."
The prolonged strength of sterling was another factor seen helping to drag the market down, traders said.

"The real problem is the strength of sterling and analysts will have to rework their earnings forecasts because of it," one trader said. "The persistence is now worrying and the damage to earnings has already been done."
UK gilts opened slightly higher but recent underperformance is set to continue ahead of the budget, dealers said. The UK Purchasing Managers Index for June could help set direction at 0830 GMT.

Among corporate features, shares in Amersham International soared in pre-market trade after the group said it planned to merge with Norway's Nycomed ASA. The shares rose 295p to 18.00 stg by 0706 GMT.
Elsewhere, shares in furniture retailer MFI were indicated five pence lower at 130p after group profits, which rose 21 percent, came at the bottom of the range of analysts' forecasts.
